hero.headline: 3 arrested in death of 3-month-old in St. Lucie County from dehydration and malnutrition
hero.teaser: Three people were arrested Friday, nearly a year after a 3-month-old child died in St. Lucie County. Nicole Maxwell, 27, the child's mother, Robert Maxwell, 61, the child's grandfa
hero.body:
Three people were arrested Friday, nearly a year after a 3-month-old child died in St. Lucie County. Nicole Maxwell, 27, the child's mother, Robert Maxwell, 61, the child's grandfather, and Vikki Koon, 38, Robert Maxwell's girlfriend, face charges in the case according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office.

 Deputies, detectives and crime scene investigators responded to Lawnwood Regional Medical Center on Aug. 20, 2025, after the 3-month-old was brought to the emergency room by the child's grandparents. The sheriff's office said medical personnel notified them that the child had been pronounced deceased and exhibited injuries and conditions consistent with possible neglect. The Medical Examiner determined the child's manner of death to be homicide, with the cause of death attributed to dehydration and malnutrition.

 Each suspect faces charges of aggravated manslaughter of a child and aggravated child abuse. Bond was set at $1.5 million for each defendant.

 Sheriff Richard Del Toro said in a statement that the death of a child is a tragedy that affects the entire community. He commended Detective Corporal Jennifer Diaz for her leadership and thanked the detectives, crime scene investigators, professional support staff, the Medical Examiner's Office and the State Attorneys whose commitment and teamwork led to the arrests.

cards.headline: Florida spiny lobster mini season opens Wednesday with strict two-day harvest window
cards.body:
Florida's spiny lobster sport season returns Wednesday, July 29 through Thursday, July 30, offering recreational divers and snorkelers a two-day opportunity to harvest the prized crustaceans. The annual event occurs on the last consecutive Wednesday and Thursday of July each year and is open to both Florida residents and non-residents. The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission enforces strict bag limits that vary by location, with Monroe County and Biscayne National Park restricted to 6 lobsters per person per day, while the rest of Florida waters allow 12 lobsters per person per day. Possession limits on the water equal the daily bag limit, while off-water possession on July 29 equals the daily bag limit and doubles on July 30 to either 12 or 24 depending on location.

All harvested spiny lobsters must meet Florida's minimum size requirement, with carapace length exceeding 3 inches when measured in water. Possession and use of an approved measuring device is mandatory at all times, and all measurements must be taken while the lobster is still in the water. Night diving is prohibited in Monroe County during the sport season only, with the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission defining diving as swimming at or below the water surface. This restriction applies exclusively to Monroe County waters during the July 29-30 sport season.

Several areas remain completely off-limits to lobster harvesting, including John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park, Everglades National Park, Dry Tortugas National Park, Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary no-take zones, Biscayne Bay/Card Sound Lobster Sanctuary, and five Coral Reef Protection Areas in Biscayne National Park. Popular diving destinations open to harvesting include Florida Keys locations outside prohibited areas, Miami-Dade County waters, Broward County reefs, and Palm Beach County diving spots. The 2026 mini season attracts thousands of recreational harvesters to these coastal locations.

Participants must possess a valid Florida saltwater fishing license, spiny lobster permit if required, approved measuring gauge, dive flag and proper safety equipment, and a cooler with ice for proper storage. According to the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, spiny lobster mini season generates significant economic activity for coastal communities while supporting conservation efforts. The strict regulations, including size limits and seasonal restrictions, help maintain healthy lobster populations for both recreational and commercial harvesting.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast home prices rise after two-year decline, with St. Lucie County up 2.3%
cards.body:
Single-family home prices are rising across the Treasure Coast after dropping from 2023 to 2025. Martin County median home sale prices are up 1.1% since 2025, sitting at $655,000. St. Lucie County is seeing the highest increase in the region, up 2.3% since June 2025 with a median sale price of $399,000. Indian River County has seen an increase of 1.8%, with a median sales price of $400,000.

Kelley Decowski, an award-winning realtor at REMAX in Stuart, said the increases are being driven by low supply and high demand. Decowski said buyers should start making decisions now because there are no signs that the prices are going to come back down and they are probably going to continue to increase. She said inventory is low on the Treasure Coast, though the market is currently balanced for both buyers and sellers.

Decowski said buyers need to be realistic with their offers and need to come in pre-approved before they go looking at homes. Sellers need to price their homes realistically and need to present a well-maintained product. For some Martin County homeowners, the rising prices are reshaping long-term plans.

Cara Collins, who bought her home before the COVID-19 pandemic when prices were significantly lower, said she has no plans to sell. Collins said this is going to be her family home as long as the market is still as high as it is. She said current prices are higher than she would hope for and that the market has changed what would be possible for her family today. Collins said she would not be able to be a stay-at-home mom and be able to afford a home for her kids if they would be buying now. Condo and townhome prices have dropped in Martin and St. Lucie counties and increased by less than a percent in Indian River County.

cards.headline: Big Taste of Martin County returns Oct. 6 in Stuart to support youth mentoring programs
cards.body:
Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties will host Big Taste of Martin County on Oct. 6 at Atlantic Aviation in Stuart. The annual fundraiser brings together local restaurants, chefs and community partners to support mentoring programs for children across the Treasure Coast.

Guests can sample food, wine and beer from area businesses while participating restaurants compete for Big Taste awards and local bragging rights. Spritz Stuart plans to feature several menu items during the event promotion, including a Tuscan salmon dish, a smash burger and a specialty cocktail called the Fig & Flame.

Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties said the event helps fund mentorship opportunities for children who are currently waiting to be matched with a mentor, known as a Big. The nonprofit serves children and families throughout Palm Beach and Martin counties through one-on-one mentoring relationships designed to support academic achievement, confidence and personal growth.

Community members can support the mission by purchasing tickets, attending the event or volunteering to become a mentor. More information about the event and mentorship opportunities is available through Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties.

cards.headline: 60 St. Lucie County teens complete summer internship program aimed at keeping young workers local
cards.teaser: A summer internship program run by the St. Lucie County Economic Development Council gave 60 students work experience at 50 local businesses. The interns graduate from the program Friday.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Economic Development Council hopes its Treasure Coast Center for Economic & Educational Development summer internship program creates a pipeline for young workers to stay on the Treasure Coast. This is the second year of the program. The program gave 60 students, ranging from rising juniors to graduated seniors, an opportunity to work at 50 local businesses in skilled trades, manufacturing, hospitality, healthcare, government and much more. The Boys and Girls Club is funding a $15 an hour stipend for students and providing financial literacy classes on Fridays.

 Two of the interns are Tylarith Limear, a 2026 graduate of Fort Pierce Central High School working at Aircraft Turbine Works at the Treasure Coast Airport, and Jeronimo Rodrigues, a 2026 graduate of St. Lucie West Centennial High School interning at the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. Anita Fischer with the St. Lucie County EDC said the program was needed because there are jobs and high-level positions on the Treasure Coast. The interns graduate from the program on Friday.

cards.headline: Martin County Fire Rescue faces $16.5M loss, 116 job cuts if property tax reform passes
cards.teaser: Martin County Fire Rescue could lose $16.5 million if voters approve property tax reform in November, according to public records. County commissioners are set to discuss what thos
cards.body:
Martin County Fire Rescue could lose $16.5 million if voters approve property tax reform in November, according to public records. County commissioners are set to discuss what those changes could mean for the fire department in a commission meeting Tuesday. The proposed reform would increase the homestead exemption over two years, and the department is bracing for the impact.

 Rick Sterl, president of the Martin County Firefighters Association, IAFF Local 2959, said most of the department's funding comes from ad-valorem and general fund revenue. If voters approve the reform, Martin County Fire Rescue's presentation outlines two stark options: cut services or cut staff. Cutting services would mean closing fire stations, ending hazmat, dive and technical rescue operations, grounding the critical care helicopter, and using firefighting equipment past its lifespan. Cutting staff would mean eliminating 116 firefighters over two years, roughly one in three firefighters in the department.

 Sterl said the consequences of either path would be felt by the public. "Any reductions is going to possibly change the outcome of the level of care the response time," said Sterl. "At the end of the day, any cuts is someone is going to pay the price." According to public records, both options create compounding problems.

 Cut services and remaining personnel can't respond properly, or cut firefighters and there won't be enough staff to maintain existing services. Fire rescue argues no version of the proposal allows the department to remain whole.

 Residents in Martin County offered mixed reactions to the potential cuts. Joe Vessichio said he doesn't believe the cuts will happen. "Neither one is going to happen, we have more than enough money," said Vessichio.

 "And even if it does, big deal, so a couple of people lose their job, they get retrained to do something else." Lisa Freitas, owner of Lisa Gay Fashions, expressed concern about what cuts could mean for public safety. "Wow, what a job they do. You can't go that route for our safety. They protect our families," said Freitas.

cards.headline: Martin and St. Lucie counties report five confirmed cases of cyclosporiasiasis
cards.teaser: The Florida Department of Health has confirmed 94 cases of cyclosporiasiasis statewide, including two in St. Lucie County, two in Palm Beach County and one in Martin County.
cards.body:
Growing outbreaks linked to bacteria and parasites on produce continue making headlines. The Florida Department of Health has confirmed 94 cases of cyclosporiasis statewide, including two in Palm Beach County, two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County.

 Ryan Boylston of Delray Beach has responded by growing his own produce in his front yard. His property includes spinach, lettuce, arugula, star fruit, bananas, peppers, pineapple and herbs that his family eats every day. Boylston started growing his own food about three years ago after struggling to find produce he felt was healthy and free of chemicals or contaminants.

 He now helps others install gardens in their own yards through his company, Urban Abundance. The other half of his property is filled with herbs and vegetables growing in raised planters similar to the ones he builds for customers. For beginners interested in starting their own garden, Boylston recommends growing crops that can handle Florida's summer heat, including spinach, sweet potatoes and yardlong beans.

 He says lettuce and tomatoes do much better during the winter months. Boylston recommends raised garden beds with smooth sides that iguanas cannot easily climb, and suggests building cages or enclosures around plants growing directly in the ground for protection.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce mother leaves nursing career as childcare costs consume 20% of household income
cards.teaser: Siedah White estimated childcare for her four children ranged from $275 per week for toddlers to $300 per week for infants, forcing her to become a full-time mom.
cards.body:
Siedah White of Fort Pierce left her job as a certified nurse assistant after childcare costs for her four children consumed approximately 20 percent of her household income. She was one of over 100 people to comment on WPTV's Facebook page about the rising cost of childcare in Florida. White said she was paying $300 per week for each infant and $275 per week for toddlers, expenses that forced her to become a full-time mom. She now hosts a video Mom blog on Instagram and TikTok.

 "I was just working just to pay childcare, and we weren't able to meet our family goals as far as needing to move into a larger place and upgrading our family vehicle," White told WPTV. The decision to leave her career came after she realized that working was not helping her family achieve their financial objectives despite bringing in additional income.

 According to the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta, childcare prices increased 29 percent from 2020 to 2024, outpacing the 22 percent rise in overall prices during the same period. Childcare costs now frequently exceed the 7 percent of income affordability benchmark established by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. The Atlanta Fed examined childcare costs in Georgia and Florida and found that 85.4 percent of Florida families are estimated to spend more than 7 percent of their income on childcare.

 The study found that the estimated weekly costs for care of infant and toddler children in Florida are $268 and $208 for preschool-aged children. The median percentage of income families would need to pay for childcare in Florida is 13.9 percent, nearly double the federal affordability benchmark. The research indicates these costs are putting significant financial pressure on parents and forcing difficult decisions about work hours and employment. Some parents, like White, are choosing to leave the workforce entirely rather than continue paying childcare expenses that consume a substantial portion of their earnings.

cards.headline: Murray Middle School demolition underway after Hurricane Milton tornado damage
cards.teaser: Murray Middle School demolition is underway in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton.
cards.body:
Murray Middle School demolition is underway in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton. The project includes reconstruction of buildings destroyed in the tornadoes, along with a new administration building, media center, art lab, and a full overhaul of the parking lot. The demolition phase alone costs $3.3 million, though the total project cost has not been finalized.

 The project is being funded by local capital improvement, sales tax and Public Education Capital Outlay. Students who were displaced from the affected classrooms will continue learning in portable classrooms until construction is complete.

 Kirstie Gernaine, coordinator of public information and community relations for the Martin County School District, said Murray Middle School was already slated to get all of this construction work with a new admin area, a new media center and a brand new art lab. With Hurricane Milton and those tornadoes destroying the buildings in the back buildings 18, 10, and nine, the district was able to add these on.

 The school district said parents can be assured their students will be safe during construction. Barriers have already been placed around the work zone to keep students out. The district hopes to complete the renovations by December 2027.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce police release body camera video of officer striking suspect during arrest
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce police released body camera video showing an officer striking a man in an incident that started when officers responded to a reported assault of a woman under the South Bridge on Tuesday.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce police released body camera video showing the moments leading up to an officer striking a man in an incident that has been circulating online. Officials said the incident started when officers responded to a reported assault of a woman under the South Bridge on Tuesday at 11:47 a.m. According to the department, officers stepped in to stop the attack, but the suspect, Justin Ikeler, 42, refused commands and raised his fists at them.

 The department said an officer then struck Ikeler to protect himself and make the arrest. Police said in a statement that when officers attempted to take Ikeler into custody, he pulled away, refused repeated commands and assumed a fighting stance with his fists raised toward the officers. Based on Ikeler's actions, the officer perceived an imminent threat of assault and delivered defensive strikes to protect himself and gain control of Ikeler so the arrest could be completed.

 Ikeler is now in the St. Lucie County Jail. The department said the investigation remains active and its release of the video is intended to provide additional context regarding the incident.

cards.headline: Community gathers to honor 9-year-old boy killed in dirt bike crash with FedEx truck in St. Lucie County
cards.teaser: Family members, friends and neighbors gathered Tuesday evening to honor the life of a 9-year-old boy killed in a crash involving a dirt bike and a FedEx box tru.
cards.body:
Family members, friends and neighbors gathered Tuesday evening to honor the life of a 9-year-old boy killed in a crash involving a dirt bike and a FedEx box truck in St. Lucie County. The vigil was held less than 24 hours after the crash on East Midway Road, where the child was pronounced dead Monday afternoon. According to the Florida Highway Patrol, the crash happened around 3:07 p.m. Monday in the 600 block of East Midway Road near Fort Pierce.

 Investigators said the 9-year-old and a 12-year-old were riding a dirt bike when it collided with a FedEx box truck. The 9-year-old died at the scene. The 12-year-old was taken to a local hospital in stable condition.

 Although the Florida Highway Patrol has not publicly released the victim's identity, loved ones came together to remember the young boy with candles, balloons and prayers. Neighbors said the area is a common place for children and others to ride bicycles and dirt bikes. The Florida Highway Patrol continues to investigate what led to the collision.

cards.headline: Palm City dog trainer trial delayed for eighth time as judge voices frustration in Martin County court
cards.teaser: Tempers flared in a Martin County courtroom Tuesday as Judge Elizabeth Metzger pressed both prosecution and defense over why the animal cruelty case against Nikki Camerlengo still hasn't gone to trial more than two years after charges were filed.
cards.body:
The hearing marked the eighth continuance in the case against Palm City dog trainer, groomer and boarder Nikki Camerlengo. Judge Elizabeth Metzger made her frustration clear from the bench, telling both legal teams the case has been continued so many times she has lost count. At one point, an exchange between the judge and Camerlengo's defense attorney, Stuart Kaplan, grew heated. When Kaplan said the delays were of no fault of the defendant, Metzger replied "I'm not saying that!" as Kaplan protested "You're looking at me!"

 Camerlengo was arrested in 2024 on two felony animal cruelty charges after Martin County detectives said two dogs died in her care. The arrest followed a WPTV investigation by Investigative Reporter Kate Hussey that linked at least seven dog deaths or serious injuries to Camerlengo's Pawsitively Paradise facility over the course of a decade. Kaplan is asking the court to block testimony from both the Texas veterinary pathologist who performed the two necropsies and from lead investigator Detective Christine Polizzi.

 Prosecutor Kristen Chase did not oppose the latest continuance, saying she is waiting on a deposition of her expert witness scheduled for July 31, delayed by scheduling conflicts. Another status hearing is set for Aug. 3, after the expert deposition.

cards.headline: Second arrest made in fatal shooting of Fort Pierce art teacher Andre Leonard Barnes
cards.teaser: Dale A. Mincey, 41, Barnes' nephew, was formally charged with first-degree murder Saturday in connection with the July 7 shooting on the 2700 block of Essex Drive.
cards.body:
The fatal shooting happened July 7 at a residence on the 2700 block of Essex Drive. Deputies responded to the home at around 3:30 p.m. after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When deputies arrived, they learned a man had shot another man with a rifle.

 Barnes was taken to a local hospital, where he died. Dale A. Mincey, 41, Barnes' nephew, was formally charged with first-degree murder Saturday in connection with Barnes' death.

 Mincey remains in custody at the St. Lucie County Jail and is being held without bond. During questioning, Mincey told detectives he could not recall what happened the day of the shooting and that he didn't have any issues with Barnes and did not know how Barnes died, an arrest affidavit said. However, he admitted to owning two firearms.

 Karen Moye, the victim's sister and mother of the suspect, was also at the home when the shooting occurred. She heard a loud bang while she was in the bathroom and came out to find Mincey and called police, an arrest affidavit said. Moye, who lived in the home with Mincey and Barnes, told detectives immediately after the shooting that the pair did not have a good relationship and that Mincey told her he was expressing fear in the days leading up to the shooting.

 Sheriff Richard Del Toro said Moye knowingly provided false information to investigators and withheld pertinent information related to this homicide investigation. She has been charged with false report to law enforcement and the commission of a capital felony. Barnes worked as an art teacher for the St. Lucie County School District since 2017, serving at West Gate K-8 and Samuel S. Gaines Academy.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County man arrested after leading Martin County deputies on 100 mph chase through Indiantown
cards.teaser: A 33-year-old man led Martin County deputies on a high-speed chase through Indiantown after driving more than 100 mph on State Road 710.
cards.body:
Deputies spotted 33-year-old Markell Tillman driving aggressively at speeds exceeding 100 mph on State Road 710, forcing other vehicles off the roadway. When deputies attempted to stop him, Tillman fled. Tillman weaved through traffic in an attempt to lose deputies before turning onto SW Martin Highway toward Palm City, where he continued to drive recklessly.

 Deputies spotted Tillman again traveling eastbound on Martin Highway near Allapattah Road. Deputies used stop sticks to disable his vehicle near I-95. Tillman then bailed out of the vehicle and attempted to flee on foot before deputies caught up with him and took him into custody.

 Tillman was arrested on charges including fleeing and eluding, aggravated fleeing with injury or damage, operating a vehicle exceeding the speed limit by 50 or more mph, driving while license suspended or revoked, obstruction without violence, and operating a vehicle at 100 or more mph. Tillman also had an out-of-county warrant at the time of his arrest. He was booked into the Martin County Jail.

Collins said current prices are higher than she would hope for, and that the market has changed what would be possible for her family today. Collins said she would not be able to be a stay-at-home mom and be able to afford a home for her kids if her family would be buying now.

Condos and townhomes are seeing a different trend. Prices have dropped in Martin and St. Lucie counties and only increased by less than a percent in Indian River County. Decowski said that buyers need to be realistic with their offers and need to come in pre-approved before they go looking at homes. Sellers need to price their homes realistically and present a well-maintained product.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast home prices rise after two-year decline, with St. Lucie County up 2.3%
cards.teaser: Single-family home prices are rising across the Treasure Coast after dropping from 2023 to 2025. Martin County median home sale prices are up 1.1% since 2025, sitting at $655,000.
cards.body:
Single-family home prices are rising across the Treasure Coast after dropping from 2023 to 2025. Martin County median home sale prices are up 1.1% since 2025, sitting at $655,000. St. Lucie County is seeing the highest increase in the region, up 2.3% since June 2025 with a median sale price of $399,000. Indian River County has seen an increase of 1.8%, with a median sales price of $400,000.

 Kelley Decowski, an award-winning realtor at REMAX in Stuart, said the increases are being driven by low supply and high demand. Decowski said buyers should start making decisions now because there are no signs that the prices are going to come back down and they are probably going to continue to increase. She said inventory is low on the Treasure Coast, though the market is currently balanced for both buyers and sellers.

 Decowski said buyers need to be realistic with their offers and need to come in pre-approved before they go looking at homes. Sellers need to price their homes realistically and need to present a well-maintained product. For some Martin County homeowners, the rising prices are reshaping long-term plans.

 Cara Collins, who bought her home before the COVID-19 pandemic when prices were significantly lower, said she has no plans to sell. Collins said this is going to be her family home as long as the market is still as high as it is. She said current prices are higher than she would hope for and that the market has changed what would be possible for her family today.

 Collins said she would not be able to be a stay-at-home mom and be able to afford a home for her kids if they would be buying now. Condo and townhome prices have dropped in Martin and St. Lucie counties and increased by less than a percent in Indian River County.

cards.headline: Private racetrack resort community breaks ground in St. Lucie County on 650 acres
cards.teaser: P1 Motor Club is under construction on 650 acres off Okeechobee Road in St. Lucie County, replacing fairways with racing circuits and preparing to welcome its first drivers this fa
cards.body:
P1 Motor Club is under construction on 650 acres off Okeechobee Road in St. Lucie County, replacing fairways with racing circuits and preparing to welcome its first drivers this fall. The private racetrack resort community features 10 miles of racing circuits designed for street cars, race cars and go-karts. Chris DuPlessis, Director of Fun for P1 Motor Club, compared the concept to a high-end golf resort, except with a racetrack instead of a golf course.

 The first track under construction is the 3-mile Treasure Coast Track, set to open in October. Over the next six months, crews will continue work on additional circuits, including the flagship 4.5-mile P1 International Circuit. DuPlessis said the club is designed for drivers of all ages and skill levels, with kids as young as 8 years old driving go-karts all the way up to grandparents still driving their cars on track, making it a family club.

 Membership comes with a $192,000 initiation fee and $12,000 in yearly dues. The club already has 260 members. Construction on a clubhouse and homes for up to 125 residents is scheduled to begin in 2027. The development will also include condos and customizable garages with living spaces situated directly along the tracks.

 Despite the scale of the project, developers say they want to preserve the character of the region by planting trees, creating lakes, and incorporating natural landscaping throughout the property. DuPlessis said it will feel like the racetrack has been there for 100 years, comparing the scope of work to building a city. P1 Motor Club is expected to be fully completed by 2028.

cards.headline: Survey finds 64% say inflation made basics harder to afford, 42% skipped medical care
cards.teaser: A 2026 survey from eHealth found 64% of those polled say inflation has made it harder to afford basics like food, housing and clothing, with 42% saying they skipped or delayed medical care in the past year.
cards.body:
A 2026 survey from eHealth found 64% of those polled say inflation has made it harder to afford basics like food, housing and clothing, forcing many Americans to make difficult choices between necessities like rent, groceries and healthcare. The study reveals that healthcare is often losing out when people are forced to prioritize their spending.

 Medicare recipients are especially finding it challenging to afford healthcare amid rising costs. Judith Waseka, who attended a Let's Hear It community event in Vero Beach, said even with supplemental help, she and her husband are having a hard time affording their prescription drugs. "You either eat or you pay for your medication, or you sell your house or you pay for your medication," Waseka said.

 The financial pressures are leading to serious consequences for people's health. Forty-two percent of those polled say they've skipped or delayed medical care in the past year because of inflation, according to the eHealth study. This means nearly half of respondents are going without needed medical attention due to cost concerns.

 The survey highlights how inflation is forcing Americans to make impossible choices between basic necessities. When stretched budgets cannot cover housing, food and medical care simultaneously, many are choosing to forgo healthcare rather than go without shelter or meals. The findings underscore the growing financial strain facing families, particularly those on Medicare who are living on fixed incomes while trying to manage healthcare expenses that continue to rise.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound couple seeks community support as husband battles head and neck cancer
cards.teaser: A Hobe Sound couple is asking for community support as they navigate a cancer diagnosis, holding onto faith every step of the way.
cards.body:
Dave and Faren Motz met in South Florida before moving to Maui, where they married and raised their family. Faren raised all three of their kids and home schooled. The couple started a business and had a farm where they served children.

 Years later, they moved to Hobe Sound and purchased a property, but just months after settling in, Dave was diagnosed with head and neck cancer. As the couple searched for the right healthcare in Florida, AdventHealth in Celebration provided programs and grants that became a critical resource.

 Dave underwent nearly seven weeks of daily radiation treatments. The repeated visits to Orlando, biopsies, scans, and exams added up, costing the couple nearly $20,000 out of pocket. Their age and income kept them from qualifying for Medicare or Medicaid.

 Dave, a former firefighter, had long been the family's provider. Now, Faren has stepped up to support them both, driving him back and forth from Orlando for treatment. Doctors told Dave he has an 85% chance of recovery.

 Faren works at Latitudes at the Jupiter Beach Resort, where those who want to show their support can stop by and visit. Those who would like to contribute financially can donate to the family's GoFundMe at Standing with Dave Motz in his cancer battle.

cards.headline: Some Villa Del Sol residents return home nearly 2 years after structural damage forced evacuation
cards.teaser: Villa Del Sol residents in St. Lucie County told WPTV they are able to return home after nearly two years of being displaced from their condos following structural damage found in August 2024.
cards.body:
Residents told WPTV they were notified last month they could return to their condos, after an inspection in August 2024 found structural damage in buildings 3, 4, and 5, which were deemed unsafe. Katie Johnson was the first to share to WPTV that residents had been told they could come back. WPTV received emails sent to residents from the Board of Directors telling them they could return.

 WPTV also obtained a letter from engineers sent to St. Lucie County's Building Department requesting they lift occupancy restrictions following their special inspection. Katie Johnson described the work still underway at the property, saying they're still moving the dirt back under the buildings.

 Robert Segedin took WPTV inside his family's home, excited to return but thinking about those who cannot. Eric Johnson is among those not coming back. He was one of the first residents WPTV met at Villa Del Sol and is now living in Georgia.

 Eric Johnson said the financial toll has been severe, explaining the family had to drain out all their savings accounts and all their 401ks just trying to make ends meet while this was going on. He is filing for bankruptcy and filing his condo for foreclosure. Katie Johnson said she is thinking of neighbors like Eric Johnson who cannot return, saying she feels so bad that some were hit harder than others with the situation.

cards.headline: JetBlue cancels Vero Beach to JFK route in September, citing low demand
cards.teaser: JetBlue is ending its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport on Sept. 9, just nine months after the route launched in December.
cards.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route. Dambeck said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates, with air carriers fluctuating based off of demand.

 Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time if the airline had stayed with it. Ahern said the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach is hard to beat because it is easy and close. All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds.

 Dambeck said JetBlue will evaluate continuously, so just because the route is gone now does not mean it will never come back. The Boston route from Vero Beach is seeing great demand, Dambeck said.

hero.headline: Treasure Coast Traffic Report: I-95 Ramp Closures and Road Work Planned July 26-31
hero.teaser:
**Drivers should prepare for overnight ramp closures at Martin Highway, Midway Road and Orange Avenue, along with extended neighborhood road closures in Port St. Lucie.**

Motorist
hero.body:
**Drivers should prepare for overnight ramp closures at Martin Highway, Midway Road and Orange Avenue, along with extended neighborhood road closures in Port St. Lucie.**

Motorists across the Treasure Coast could encounter delays during the week of July 24-31 as construction and maintenance continue on major roadways in Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

The Florida Department of Transportation's latest weekly traffic report highlights several full road and ramp closures expected to have the greatest effect on drivers.

## Major closures to know about

### Three I-95 ramps at Martin Highway closing overnight

Three ramps serving Martin Highway at Interstate 95 will close overnight from Sunday, July 26, through Thursday, July 30.

The northbound I-95 exit ramp to Martin Highway at Exit 110 will be closed from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Drivers will continue north to Becker Road at Exit 114, travel west on Becker Road and use southbound I-95 to return to the Martin Highway exit.

The northbound I-95 entrance ramp from Martin Highway will also close during the same hours. Motorists will be detoured east on Martin Highway, north on Newfield Parkway and west on Becker Road to reach northbound I-95.

The southbound I-95 exit ramp to Martin Highway at Exit 110 will also close overnight. Drivers will be directed to exit at High Meadow Avenue at Exit 102, travel north on High Meadow Avenue and continue to Martin Highway.

FDOT said only one ramp closure will occur at a time.

### All four Midway Road ramps scheduled for overnight closures

All four I-95 ramps at Midway Road are scheduled to close separately from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 26, through Friday, July 31, for paving.

The northbound entrance ramp from Midway Road will close, with traffic directed south on I-95 to St. Lucie West Boulevard before returning to northbound I-95.

The northbound exit ramp to Midway Road will close, with drivers detoured through St. Lucie West Boulevard, Prima Vista Boulevard and U.S. 1.

The southbound exit ramp to Midway Road will close, with motorists directed to St. Lucie West Boulevard before returning north on I-95 to Exit 126.

The southbound entrance ramp from Midway Road will also close. Drivers will be directed east on Midway Road, south on U.S. 1 and west on St. Lucie West Boulevard to reach southbound I-95.

Only one ramp will be closed at a time.

### Orange Avenue exit closing in Fort Pierce

The northbound I-95 exit ramp to westbound State Road 68, or Orange Avenue, will be closed from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 26, through Thursday, July 30.

Motorists will be detoured to the eastbound Orange Avenue exit, north on Jenkins Road and west on Loop Road before returning to westbound Orange Avenue.

The closure is needed for paving and lighting installation.

## Port St. Lucie neighborhood roads may close for several days

Extended closures are planned along several streets near the SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard widening project.

Closures may begin at 7 a.m. Monday, July 27, and continue until 5 p.m. Friday, July 31, on portions of:

- SW Jaslo Avenue
- SW Jacoby Avenue
- SW McCullough Avenue
- SW McCall Road
- SW McHord Avenue
- SW Paar Drive

The closures are needed for drainage and utility installation. Adjacent roads will not close at the same time, and access to homes and businesses will be maintained.

Detours will use nearby roads including SW McCain Street, SW McIntyre Street, SW Kabane Street, SW Jordin Avenue and SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard.

## Martin County traffic impacts

Northbound and southbound I-95 between Bridge Road and the Martin-St. Lucie county line will have two lanes closed overnight for milling, resurfacing and signage work.

U.S. 1 between Fischer Street and Decker Avenue may have two lanes closed intermittently from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday through Friday for sign installation.

A1A between Shore Village Terrace and the Jensen Beach Causeway may be reduced to one lane at times Monday through Friday for pavement widening and drainage work. Flaggers will maintain two-way traffic.

Martin Highway between Stuart West Boulevard and Citrus Boulevard may have intermittent overnight lane closures Tuesday through Thursday.

In Stuart, two westbound lanes on Monterey Road between Ocean Boulevard and Monterey Commons Boulevard may close overnight Monday through Wednesday. Kanner Highway between Lost River Road and Jack James Drive may also have overnight lane closures Wednesday through Friday.

## St. Lucie County traffic impacts

Northbound I-95 between Gatlin Boulevard and Becker Road will have two lanes closed overnight Sunday through Friday for milling and repaving.

Port St. Lucie Boulevard between Seafury Lane and Lennard Road may have daytime lane closures Monday through Friday. Two lanes may close overnight for drainage work, milling and repaving.

U.S. 1 between Jennings Road and Golden Oak Trail may also have lane restrictions during daytime and overnight hours.

SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard between Jordin Avenue and Alcantarra Boulevard will have intermittent daytime lane closures for roadway construction.

Up to two lanes may close overnight on I-95 between Glades Cut-Off Road and the area just south of Okeechobee Road.

Midway Road between Florida's Turnpike and Selvitz Road will continue to have intermittent weekday lane closures as part of the widening project.

## North Causeway marine closure planned in August

Boaters should also be aware of a temporary change to operations at the former North Causeway drawbridge in Fort Pierce from Aug. 3-8.

The navigation channel will be fully obstructed from 7 a.m. Aug. 3 through 7 a.m. Aug. 6.

Single-leaf openings will then be available during portions of Aug. 6, 7 and 8, although the channel will be completely closed for two-hour periods while crews remove steel bascule leaves.

FDOT said there will be no impact to vehicle traffic on the new North Causeway Bridge.

## Indian River County traffic impacts

One lane may remain closed on the 17th Street bridges between Indian River Boulevard and Indian Bay Drive as bridge rehabilitation continues.

I-95 near the new Oslo Road interchange may have one or two lanes closed overnight Sunday through Thursday for bridge work, milling and resurfacing.

On 90th Avenue between Sebastian Boulevard and 87th Street, one lane may close overnight Sunday through Friday for roadway construction.

Drivers near Sebastian Inlet should expect intermittent lane and shoulder closures on A1A through August. Flaggers will direct traffic through the work zone.

Sections of the north and south parking lots at Sebastian Inlet State Park remain closed during construction of the replacement bridge. The park, boat ramp and portions of both parking areas remain open.

Construction schedules may change because of weather or other unforeseen conditions. Drivers should allow additional travel time, follow posted detours and use caution around workers and equipment.

Real-time I-95 traffic information is available through Florida 511, while updated lane closure information is available through FDOT District Four.

cards.headline: Messi bathed Yamal as baby in 2007 photo shoot, now they meet in World Cup final
cards.teaser: A 2007 charity calendar photo shoot paired teenage Lionel Messi with infant Lamine Yamal. Now 19 years later, they face off in Sunday's World Cup final.
cards.body:
Photographer Joan Monfort took photos in 2007 of a teenage Lionel Messi bathing infant Lamine Yamal in a plastic bathtub as part of a charity calendar produced by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF. Monfort, who works as a freelance photojournalist for The Associated Press, took the photos after Yamal's mother won a raffle of families in the city of Mataró near Barcelona who wanted to participate.

 Soccer destiny paired her baby boy with the Argentine who would become the greatest of all time. Messi left Barcelona in 2021 when the club was in financial trouble. Yamal erupted at the club two years later.

 Monfort had no recollection of the photos until Yamal's father posted one on social media during the 2024 European Championship, when a teenage Yamal led Spain to the title. The photo went viral then, but interest has skyrocketed with Sunday's World Cup final between Argentina and Spain approaching. Monfort said he has been bombarded by queries for the photos by professional media outlets while also seeing his images reproduced countless times on social media and the internet without any credit or compensation.

 The 19-year-old Yamal will face a Messi who is 20 years his senior in Sunday's final. Monfort, 58, is considering traveling to see the final in New Jersey. He said his heart is split and he does not know if he wants Messi or Yamal to win.

cards.headline: President Trump to Attend World Cup Final in New Jersey with Stepped-Up Security
cards.teaser: The World Cup final Sunday in New Jersey has been designated a Level 1 Special Event with President Trump attending the trophy presentation and enhanced security from multiple federal agencies.
cards.body:
The 2026 FIFA World Cup began with 48 teams playing over 39 days. Now it comes down to one final match Sunday in New Jersey. As Argentina and Spain prepare to take the pitch, a sprawling network of federal agents, local law enforcement, and private companies continue with a game plan two years in the making to ensure the final is safe.

 A joint operations center in New York has helped oversee security and monitor threats in host cities throughout the tournament, with thousands of personnel on the ground and a team with an eye on the skies. The FBI has seized hundreds of drones flying in restricted airspace near stadiums during the tournament.

 The final will include a beefed-up Secret Service perimeter, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt says his attendance will cap what has been the most watched, most secure, and most successful World Cup in American history. When Trump attended an NBA Finals game last month in New York, police shut down several city blocks around the arena and fans were forced to wait in extra-long lines to go through enhanced security.

 The World Cup final is a Level 1 Special Event, the highest possible security designation, with added resources from the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense, and the FBI. No one will be allowed to simply walk up to the stadium or drive a personal vehicle.

cards.headline: Major League Baseball Restricts iPad Use in Dugouts to Block AI Decision-Making
cards.teaser: MLB has made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible starting Wednesday to prevent teams from using artificial intelligence to make in-game decisions about substitutions and pitch calling.
cards.body:
Major League Baseball is restricting iPad usage in dugouts to prevent the tablets from running artificial intelligence to help make decisions. The tablets have access to video and league-provided data, and also included a custom tab where teams could access other programs. MLB made the custom tabs inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night, when the second half of the season started.

 MLB executive vice president of baseball operations Morgan Sword wrote in a June 11 memo to general managers, assistant GMs and video coordinators that in many cases, the custom tab had expanded the use of the dugout iPads beyond their originally intended purpose to include recommendations regarding substitutions, pitch calling, and other in-game decisions traditionally made by players and coaches. The memo was first reported by The Athletic and was obtained by The Associated Press.

 A review by the competition committee found clubs had been compliant with the regulations. Sword wrote that instituting this prohibition beginning with the second half of the season is intended to provide clubs that have relied on the custom tab with appropriate lead-time to make any necessary adjustments. MLB started a pilot program allowing use of iPads in dugouts with restrictions late in the 2015 season and expanded their use in 2016 under a deal with Apple. Video was eliminated in the 2020 COVID season following the Houston Astros' sign-stealing scandal, then returned in 2021.

cards.headline: Britain's Josh Kerr breaks mile world record with 3:42.66 run in London
cards.teaser: Josh Kerr shattered a 27-year-old world record on Saturday, running the mile in 3:42.66 at a Diamond League event in London.
cards.body:
Great Britain's Josh Kerr ran the mile in 3:42.66 on Saturday in London, breaking Hicham El Guerrouj's previous mark of 3:43.13 set in 1999. The 27-year-old made no secret that he was targeting the long-standing record at Saturday's Diamond League event in London. Earlier this week, he revealed he ran 2:42.45 in a 1,200-meter time trial.

 His sponsor, Brooks, dubbed the effort "Project 222," referencing the number of seconds in 3 minutes, 42 seconds. American Yared Nuguse finished second in 3:45.69.

 Kerr has emerged as one of the world's top middle-distance runners, winning bronze in the 1,500 meters at the Tokyo Olympics and silver at the 2024 Paris Olympics. Before turning professional, Kerr starred at the University of New Mexico, where he won multiple NCAA titles. He also set an NCAA indoor mile record of 3:35.01 in 2018. Kerr's record-setting run came during the Diamond League, an established international circuit of professional track and field events.

cards.headline: Spain defeats Argentina 1-0 to win 2026 World Cup in extra time thriller
cards.teaser: Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 on Sunday to win the 2026 FIFA World Cup championship. Ferran Torres scored the winning goal in the 106th minute of extra time, burying a left-footed s
cards.body:
Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 on Sunday to win the 2026 FIFA World Cup championship. Ferran Torres scored the winning goal in the 106th minute of extra time, burying a left-footed shot just under the crossbar after pouncing on a bouncing ball in the box. It is Spain's second World Cup championship and first since 2010.

 Spain was absolutely dominant throughout the match in terms of possession and shot attempts. The team took 15 shots in regulation while Argentina managed none. Spain also won nine corners compared to Argentina's single corner kick.

 Despite this overwhelming advantage, Lionel Messi and Argentina found a way to hang on and force the match into extra time. Torres broke through in the opening moment of the second 15-minute period of extra time to finally secure the victory for Spain.

 Argentina's task became even more difficult when Enzo Fernandez was sent off in second-half stoppage time after receiving his second yellow card. Fernandez was carded for a reckless play that sent Spain defender Pau Cubarsi cartwheeling into the air, forcing Argentina to finish the match with only 10 players. About two minutes after play resumed, another foul gave Lamine Yamal a chance to seal the victory from about 22 yards out on a free kick.

 His curling strike toward the right post was saved by Argentina goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez, who made a diving stop for his 10th save of the afternoon, the most ever recorded in a World Cup final. Martinez leaped to his feet afterward, punching the air and encouraging the crowd to get loud before the match eventually went to extra time.

 With the victory, Spain became the first nation to simultaneously hold the World Cup crowns in both men's and women's soccer. The final was the 104th and last match of the expanded 48-team tournament played across the United States, Canada and Mexico. Because there were more matches than any previous World Cup, the tournament produced 308 total goals, more than any other edition in history. According to FIFA, the 2026 World Cup was officially the most attended ever.

cards.headline: Flip City Gym and Cheer gymnasts earn top 15 national finish, qualify for Junior Olympics
cards.teaser: Three gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer secured a top 15 finish at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee last month and qualified for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Sk
cards.body:
Three gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer secured a top 15 finish at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee last month and qualified for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Skylar Rose-Daris, Victoria Supan, and Charli Rine represented the gym at the national competition and will advance to compete at the higher level. The trio each discovered gymnastics through unique experiences, with Rose-Daris crediting her ability to do a cartwheel, Supan finding inspiration from watching gymnasts on YouTube, and Rine enjoying the opportunity to continuously learn new skills.

 Head Coach Candice Lazuka praised the team's performance throughout the season, noting they competed at local meets before advancing through states and regionals to reach nationals. At the AAU Nationals competition in Knoxville, the team delivered an exceptional performance that nearly achieved a perfect score. Lazuka explained that earning a perfect 10 is extremely difficult, but the gymnasts managed to score a 9.9, coming very close to perfection. The strong showing at nationals secured their qualification for the Junior Olympics.

 The three gymnasts expressed excitement about the upcoming opportunity to compete at the Junior Olympics in Iowa. Rose-Daris said it's going to be really fun that she's going to an entire different part of the world. Supan described her feelings about the achievement, saying it's happy and exciting at the same time. The young athletes are preparing to take on competitors from across the country at the prestigious event.

 Looking ahead to the Junior Olympics competition, the gymnasts are setting their goals and focusing on specific events. When asked what she is focused on heading into the Junior Olympics, Rine said getting first place on floors. The qualification represents a significant achievement for both the individual gymnasts and Flip City Gym and Cheer as a whole.

 The team's progression from local competitions through the state and regional levels to nationals, and now to the Junior Olympics, demonstrates the dedication and skill development that Lazuka has cultivated in her athletes. The upcoming competition in Iowa will provide Rose-Daris, Supan, and Rine the chance to test themselves against the nation's top junior gymnasts.

hero.headline: Big Taste of Martin County returns Oct. 6 in Stuart to support youth mentoring programs
hero.body:
Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties will host Big Taste of Martin County on Oct. 6 at Atlantic Aviation in Stuart. The annual fundraiser brings together local restaurants, chefs and community partners to support mentoring programs for children across the Treasure Coast.

Guests can sample food, wine and beer from area businesses while participating restaurants compete for Big Taste awards and local bragging rights. Spritz Stuart plans to feature several menu items during the event promotion, including a Tuscan salmon dish, a smash burger and a specialty cocktail called the Fig & Flame.

Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties said the event helps fund mentorship opportunities for children who are currently waiting to be matched with a mentor, known as a Big. The nonprofit serves children and families throughout Palm Beach and Martin counties through one-on-one mentoring relationships designed to support academic achievement, confidence and personal growth.

Community members can support the mission by purchasing tickets, attending the event or volunteering to become a mentor. More information about the event and mentorship opportunities is available through Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties.

cards.headline: Boca Raton TLC Program Offers Summer Service Projects for South Florida Families
cards.teaser: B'nai Torah Congregation's TLC Program connects volunteers with hands-on service projects ranging from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking and literacy efforts.
cards.body:
B'nai Torah Congregation's TLC Program is offering South Florida families a range of hands-on service projects this summer, from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking, literacy efforts and care for seniors. Led by Summer Faerman, the program connects volunteers of all ages with mitzvah opportunities, or meaningful good deeds, as part of the congregation's broader community outreach efforts.

 The TLC Program stands for Tzedakah, Learning and Chesed, and has made service a central part of synagogue life since 2012. The program provides a way for individuals and families to put Jewish values into action while helping people in need across South Florida. It addresses multiple community concerns including hunger, homelessness, literacy, elder care, vulnerable populations and special needs. Organizers emphasize that the projects are open to everyone in the community, not only members of B'nai Torah Congregation, with the goal of making service practical, welcoming and easy to begin.

 Participants can volunteer in various ways throughout the summer. Projects include making sandwiches, serving meals, collecting and cleaning shoes, stocking Little Free Pantries, preparing backpacks for back-to-school efforts, creating Bags of Hope and helping seniors with technology. Organizers plan to demonstrate volunteer projects such as wrapping presents, making flower arrangements, preparing sandwiches, collecting shoes and assembling supplies for people in need. The variety of options allows families to choose activities that match their interests and schedules.

 As summer continues, the TLC Program offers families a way to stay connected, teach children about giving back and support neighbors throughout South Florida. B'nai Torah Congregation says the program is built around the idea that small acts of service can strengthen the larger community. More information about the TLC Program is available through B'nai Torah Congregation's website.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County Food Bank serves 2,500 hot meals daily to children at 35 summer sites
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach County Food Bank in Lake Worth Beach is serving approximately 2,500 hot meals each day to nearly 1,250 children through Florida's Summer BreakSpot program while school is out.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach County Food Bank is serving approximately 2,500 hot meals each day to nearly 1,250 children through Florida's Summer BreakSpot program, according to Food Bank leaders. The nonprofit organization supports more than 35 Summer BreakSpot sites across Palm Beach County while school is out for the summer. During a live Shining A Light broadcast on WPTV, CEO Jamie Kendall and Culinary Director Chef Doug Barg gave viewers a behind-the-scenes look inside the Michelle Hagerty Community Kitchen, where meals are prepared and loaded onto trucks for early morning deliveries across the county.

 The organization prepared more than 36,000 hot meals in June alone. According to the Palm Beach County Food Bank, hunger doesn't take a summer break, highlighting the need for continued support during the summer months. The Summer BreakSpot program provides free meals to children and teens 18 and younger during the summer when school cafeterias are closed. Food Bank leaders said the meals are distributed through partner locations across Palm Beach County to help families facing food insecurity during the summer. Kendall said the Food Bank's partnership with Summer BreakSpot helps ensure children continue receiving nutritious meals while school is out.

 During the broadcast, viewers got a close look at the large-scale kitchen operation responsible for preparing meals daily. Chef Barg walked viewers through the food production process, showing how culinary teams prepare, package and organize meals before they are loaded onto delivery trucks. The loading dock operation featured drivers and volunteers preparing for morning deliveries to Summer BreakSpot sites throughout Palm Beach County. The Palm Beach County Food Bank said volunteers and community support are critical to maintaining the program during the busy summer season.

 The Palm Beach County Food Bank is located at 701 Boutwell Road, Suite A-1, in Lake Worth Beach. Food Bank leaders said the organization continues seeking volunteers, donations and community partnerships to support its mission of reducing childhood hunger in Palm Beach County. Families looking for Summer BreakSpot meal locations can find participating sites throughout the county during the summer months.

cards.headline: Downtown Delray Beach launches Wellness Pass with free fitness classes and spa deals for July and August
cards.teaser: The Delray Beach Downtown Development Authority launched the Downtown Delray Wellness Pass for July and August. The mobile-exclusive pass allows users to access complimentary classes, discounted wellness treatments and promotions from participating businesses.
cards.body:
Downtown Delray Beach is encouraging residents and visitors to prioritize health and self-care this summer through a new Wellness Pass featuring free fitness classes, yoga sessions, spa discounts and wellness-focused offers across the city's downtown district. The Delray Beach Downtown Development Authority launched the Downtown Delray Wellness Pass for July and August.

 According to the DDA, the mobile-exclusive pass allows users to access complimentary classes, discounted wellness treatments and promotions from participating businesses throughout Downtown Delray Beach. The pass does not require an app download. Miller Physical Therapy is also participating with wellness-related services and promotions. hero.headline: Florida spiny lobster mini season opens Wednesday with strict two-day harvest window
hero.body:
Florida's spiny lobster sport season returns Wednesday, July 29 through Thursday, July 30, offering recreational divers and snorkelers a two-day opportunity to harvest the prized crustaceans. The annual event occurs on the last consecutive Wednesday and Thursday of July each year and is open to both Florida residents and non-residents. The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission enforces strict bag limits that vary by location, with Monroe County and Biscayne National Park restricted to 6 lobsters per person per day, while the rest of Florida waters allow 12 lobsters per person per day. Possession limits on the water equal the daily bag limit, while off-water possession on July 29 equals the daily bag limit and doubles on July 30 to either 12 or 24 depending on location.

All harvested spiny lobsters must meet Florida's minimum size requirement, with carapace length exceeding 3 inches when measured in water. Possession and use of an approved measuring device is mandatory at all times, and all measurements must be taken while the lobster is still in the water. Night diving is prohibited in Monroe County during the sport season only, with the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission defining diving as swimming at or below the water surface. This restriction applies exclusively to Monroe County waters during the July 29-30 sport season.

Several areas remain completely off-limits to lobster harvesting, including John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park, Everglades National Park, Dry Tortugas National Park, Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary no-take zones, Biscayne Bay/Card Sound Lobster Sanctuary, and five Coral Reef Protection Areas in Biscayne National Park. Popular diving destinations open to harvesting include Florida Keys locations outside prohibited areas, Miami-Dade County waters, Broward County reefs, and Palm Beach County diving spots. The 2026 mini season attracts thousands of recreational harvesters to these coastal locations.

Participants must possess a valid Florida saltwater fishing license, spiny lobster permit if required, approved measuring gauge, dive flag and proper safety equipment, and a cooler with ice for proper storage. According to the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, spiny lobster mini season generates significant economic activity for coastal communities while supporting conservation efforts. The strict regulations, including size limits and seasonal restrictions, help maintain healthy lobster populations for both recreational and commercial harvesting.

Florida credit card holders are taking about a year to pay off their debt, according to a WalletHub study that placed the state 30th among states where it takes the longest to eliminate credit card balances. The typical Florida cardholder carries $3,087 in credit card debt and pays nearly $350 in interest charges while working to pay it off. The analysis found it takes the average Floridian 12 months to become debt-free from their credit cards.

The findings come as Americans nationwide are struggling with mounting credit card debt, with experts projecting total U.S. credit card debt will reach approximately $100 billion this year. For Florida families already dealing with rising costs of living, the data highlights the growing financial pressure many households face when managing everyday expenses on credit.

**Drivers should prepare for overnight ramp closures at Martin Highway, Midway Road and Orange Avenue, along with extended neighborhood road closures in Port St. Lucie.**

Motorists across the Treasure Coast could encounter delays during the week of July 24-31 as construction and maintenance continue on major roadways in Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

The Florida Department of Transportation's latest weekly traffic report highlights several full road and ramp closures expected to have the greatest effect on drivers.

The southbound I-95 exit ramp to Martin Highway at Exit 110 will also close overnight. Drivers will be directed to exit at High Meadow Avenue at Exit 102, travel north on High Meadow Avenue and continue to Martin Highway.

All four I-95 ramps at Midway Road are scheduled to close separately from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 26, through Friday, July 31, for paving.

The southbound entrance ramp from Midway Road will also close. Drivers will be directed east on Midway Road, south on U.S. 1 and west on St. Lucie West Boulevard to reach southbound I-95.

cards.headline: Health insurers reverse denials after media scrutiny, raising questions about approval process
cards.teaser: Florida patients denied coverage for cancer treatments, surgeries, and medications have seen denials reversed only after journalists began investigating their cases, with insurers offering no explanation for the sudden changes.
cards.body:
Since 2025, Florida patients denied insurance coverage for doctor-recommended procedures have had those denials reversed only after media scrutiny, with no explanation from insurers. Madeline Rogers of Zephyrhills was denied coverage for colon surgery three times, Mary Barnes, a breast cancer patient in St. Pete, was forced to halt chemotherapy treatments, and Broxley Bunt of West Palm Beach was denied coverage for surgery to remove a brain tumor. In each case, the denial was reversed only after reporting began.

 United Healthcare reversed coverage for Barnes' breast cancer chemotherapy treatments after originally claiming her doctor-recommended treatments, which included immunotherapy, do not meet national cancer guidelines. The company then changed the designation to medically necessary. Dr. Bill Hennessey, a physician turned patient advocate, said denials are reversed when patients are correct and complain. Hennessey attributed the reversals to the power of the press, stating insurers do not want negative public relations.

 Federal data recently analyzed by KFF found most health insurance claims are ultimately approved, but the data does not show how many claims are denied first since insurers only report the final outcome. Most patients who are denied never appeal. A spokesperson for AHIP, the nation's largest health insurance trade group, provided a statement but offered no specific explanation for why denials are reversed after media contact.

cards.headline: Python hunters train at Everglades park ahead of Florida Python Challenge
cards.teaser: Holiday Everglades Park hosted python capture training this week as Florida prepares for its annual Python Challenge, teaching participants how to safely track and capture Burmese
cards.body:
Holiday Everglades Park hosted python capture training this week as Florida prepares for its annual Python Challenge, teaching participants how to safely track and capture Burmese pythons in the Everglades. Instructors wasted no time explaining why Burmese pythons have become such a serious problem, discussing how these massive snakes prey on native wildlife and disrupt one of the world's most unique ecosystems.

 The training emphasized that python removal efforts serve conservation purposes rather than trophies or adventure, aiming to protect Florida's natural resources. The program focused heavily on safety protocols, proper snake identification, and humane handling techniques for invasive pythons, following the official Florida Python Challenge training curriculum.

 The hands-on portion of the training proved particularly valuable as experienced handlers demonstrated proper capture techniques. Participants watched professionals show how to safely approach, control, and secure large pythons while learning that every movement has a purpose. The instructors stressed that confidence comes from training rather than taking unnecessary risks. Observing these professionals work helped participants appreciate just how strong and unpredictable these snakes can be, preparing them for the challenges they would face in actual python hunting situations.

 The training took place amid the active Everglades environment, where airboats buzzed across the marsh, alligators rested along the shoreline, and birds circled overhead. The natural surroundings reinforced the importance of protecting this incredible ecosystem and understanding that every invasive python removed can make a difference for native wildlife. The immersive setting provided participants with a realistic preview of the conditions they would encounter when searching for pythons in the vast wilderness area.

 The program left participants with a deeper respect for the men and women who spend countless hours searching the Everglades, often at night, looking for snakes that are masters of camouflage. The training session equipped volunteers with far more knowledge than they arrived with, providing them with a firsthand look at the dedication required to help preserve one of America's most remarkable wilderness areas. By preparing hunters to understand both the challenging nature of the work and the conservation significance behind it, Holiday Everglades Park's training program aims to ready participants for safely contributing to the state's ongoing efforts to remove invasive pythons and protect native wildlife in the Everglades.

cards.headline: South Florida Cost of Living Surpasses New York City as Housing Drives Affordability Crisis
cards.teaser: A new Bloomberg report shows the cost of living in the Miami-Fort Lauderdale-West Palm Beach metro area has surpassed New York City, with housing among the key drivers. The report
cards.body:
A new Bloomberg report shows the cost of living in the Miami-Fort Lauderdale-West Palm Beach metro area has surpassed New York City, with housing among the key drivers. The report cited U.S. government data showing South Florida now ranks higher than New York City in overall living costs, creating an affordability crisis that residents say they are feeling across the region.

 Wages remain a central part of the affordability problem. According to Indeed, registered nurses in South Florida earn an average of $36 an hour, compared to $56 an hour in New York. Attorneys in South Florida start around $116,000 a year, while those in New York start around $161,000. The wage disparity means South Florida residents face higher living costs while earning significantly less than their New York counterparts in comparable positions.

 Residents say they have noticed the dramatic change in recent years. Aspiring lawyer Hansell Martinez, who spoke with WPTV in West Palm Beach on Thursday, said the shift has been obvious. "From what's happened in the last five years and all the big buildings coming up and all the people coming down from New York, it has changed; things are much more expensive down here," Martinez said.

 A man visiting from Canada raised concerns about the rapid pace of growth in the region. "Where there is more concern is how much development is going on; can you sustain the development?" he said.

 The Bloomberg report sparked hundreds of comments on WPTV's Facebook page following the station's initial coverage on Wednesday, with South Florida residents expressing their concerns about rising costs. The debate over the cost of living between New York and Florida is likely to continue, but for Floridians, affordability remains the central issue as they navigate housing payments, grocery bills, and other household expenses in a market where costs have climbed above those in one of America's traditionally most expensive cities.

cards.headline: Mexican tourist killed in St. Augustine after fleeing ICE agents had valid visa, officials say
cards.teaser: Juan Jairo Coronilla Durán, a 28-year-old Mexican man killed July 14 after running from federal immigration officers in St. Augustine, was vacationing in the United States on a tou
cards.body:
Juan Jairo Coronilla Durán, a 28-year-old Mexican man killed July 14 after running from federal immigration officers in St. Augustine, was vacationing in the United States on a tourist visa, according to a Mexican official and a group assisting his wife. Coronilla Durán died after he darted across a busy road and into the path of a tractor-trailer. His death was the third in roughly a week involving encounters with Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents, following fatal shootings in Texas and Maine.

 Coronilla Durán traveled from his hometown of San Luis de la Paz in the central Mexican state of Guanajuato to Atlanta to visit family and friends, according to Isaret Jeffers, founder of Colectivo Arbol, a farmworkers advocacy group. He had stayed in Georgia for three weeks before traveling to Florida's east coast to enjoy the beaches. Yezzika Alamilla, his wife, told the organization he had been visiting on a tourist visa.

 "His wife said he was there on a tourist visa. She didn't understand what was happening," Jeffers said. "He didn't come to work; he wasn't working.

 He was here as a tourist." Alamilla "thinks he was very afraid, and that's why he ran away," Jeffers said. The Department of Homeland Security did not immediately respond to a request for comment about whether Coronilla Durán had a valid visa.

 Coronilla Durán was one of four people in a vehicle that stopped in a gas station parking lot before 7 a.m. The four fled on foot during an encounter with agents from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Homeland Security Investigations, with one darting across a busy road into the path of the semi, the Florida Highway Patrol said. The Highway Patrol and DHS have not provided additional details, citing the ongoing investigation.

 What prompted the encounter and what happened to the vehicle's other three occupants remains unclear. Alamilla called Colectivo Arbol, which provides legal advice and assistance to farmworkers in Central Florida, the day after her husband died seeking help to travel from Mexico and repatriate her husband's remains. The organization bought her a plane ticket and put her up for three days.

 Susana Guerra Vallejo, the undersecretary for assistance to migrants and mobility issues for Guanajuato, confirmed that Coronilla Durán had been in the United States for only a very short time and had a tourist visa. Coronilla Durán's body will be transported to Mexico on a commercial flight from Orlando and buried in his hometown, a farming community about 160 miles northwest of Mexico City.

 He and Alamilla had two children, a 7-month-old girl and a 7-year-old boy. His death was at least the 10th involving encounters with immigration agents since President Donald Trump launched his mass deportation campaign last year. The Mexican government has asked state attorneys general in the U.S. to review the deaths of migrants in ICE custody or during raids for possible criminal prosecution.
